name: turtle
comment: The Prism's Turtle reader (app/src/PrismSenses.lex.tex, prismTurtleDispatch) held to the W3C RDF Working Group's Turtle test suite. 'suite' pins the suite's archive as W3C serves it; 'tests' lists all 291 tests of its manifest, each file pinned by SHA-256, with the verdict the suite gives it: a positive syntax test is accepted, a negative syntax or negative evaluation test is refused, and an evaluation test reads into the same graph as its N-Triples result. A request is 'suite', a line break, the suite's home IRI, a line break, then tests in the manifest's order: each a line of the suite's verdict, the file's name and the lengths of its Turtle and of its N-Triples result (0 when it has none), then those files' bytes. The reader reads each file against its retrieval IRI (the home and the file's name: RFC 3986 section 5.1.3, as the suite's README says) and answers 'pass' and the number of tests, or 'fail', the index of the first test whose verdict differs, its file and what the reader found. Two graphs are the same when one naming of their blank nodes makes their triples equal; the reader tries the naming by order met, forwards and backwards, which settles every graph of the suite. 'examples' here hold the 159 syntax and negative evaluation tests, the acceptance vectors of the guest 'turtle'; eval/spec.json and eval2/spec.json carry the 132 evaluation tests as the vectors of 'turtle-eval' and 'turtle-eval-2', built from the same module, because one build holds about 30 KB of vectors. The examples were written from the archive by a tool kept outside the repository (project files, nervous/turtle-tool/mkspec.py); a LexLean generator that reads the archive is not written yet.
